items.title: The Good, the Bad and the Cringe: 10 Ads That Defined the Midterms
items.author: Shane Goldmacher and Tim Balk
items.content: <article>In a Democratic landslide election, here are the ads that stood out. Some were effective, while others backfired.</article>

items.title: He’ll Be Clerk of One of the Country’s Largest Counties. He’s 19.
items.author: Mack Liederman
items.content: <article>Sebastian Matta, a sophomore at Arizona State University, was elected on Tuesday as Superior Court clerk in Maricopa County, Ariz.</article>

items.title: Mysterious Request Scrambles Major Supreme Court Gun Case Against Cook County
items.author: Abbie VanSickle
items.content: <article>In an unusual move, the lead plaintiff in one of two cases challenging semiautomatic weapons bans has asked to drop out weeks before the cases are heard.</article>

items.title: Democrats, Newly Ascendant, Begin a Fight to Shape the Party’s Future
items.author: Lisa Lerer and Reid J. Epstein
items.content: <article>At a moment of opportunity for the party, its long-feuding factions are seizing on the midterm results to make their case for tacking to the center or to the left.</article>

items.title: U.S. Cleared Nvidia Chips to Chinese Firms With Empty Offices and Troubling Ties
items.author: Ana Swanson, Kalley Huang and Keith Bradsher
items.content: <article>The Commerce Department has approved dozens of Chinese companies to handle Nvidia’s H200 chips, some of which have ties to firms under sanctions over national security.</article>

items.title: With So Much New Blood in the Senate, the Average Age Is Falling. To 63.
items.author: Francesca Paris and C.J. Robinson
items.content: <article>Incoming senators are nearly 15 years younger than departing ones, on average. But the chamber’s overall age isn’t shifting much.</article>

items.title: U.S. Homeless Population Had Record Drop in 2025
items.author: Jason DeParle
items.content: <article>The Department of Housing and Urban Development credited President Trump, while homeless advocacy groups said that so-called Housing First policies of his predecessors played a part.</article>

items.title: Trump’s D.C. Construction Blitz May Be About to Get Tougher
items.author: Luke Broadwater and Emily Badger
items.content: <article>The president has bulldozed through obstacles as he has sought to remake the face of Washington. But newly empowered Democrats and angry judges are setting up a high-stakes showdown.</article>

items.title: What to Know About Stephen Miller, Trump’s New Chief of Staff
items.author: Chris Cameron
items.content: <article>The architect of President Trump’s mass deportation campaign, Mr. Miller has been the public face of many of Mr. Trump’s immigration policies.</article>

items.title: China’s Top Spy Agency Recruited Woman Who Targeted Jensen Huang
items.author: Julian E. Barnes, Tripp Mickle, Paul Mozur and Maggie Haberman
items.content: <article>A memo that circulated among U.S. policymakers cited intelligence that Alice Huang, a Chinese executive who developed a relationship with Nvidia’s leader, was an asset of Beijing’s Ministry of State Security.</article>

items.title: In Elevating Stephen Miller, Trump Doubles Down on Hard-Line Agenda
items.author: Maggie Haberman, Jonathan Swan and Tyler Pager
items.content: <article>The new White House chief of staff is responsible for some of the most provocative policies of President Trump’s second term, as well as an aggressive approach to executive power.</article>

items.title: Susie Wiles Is the Latest Powerful Woman to Exit the Trump Administration
items.author: Chris Cameron
items.content: <article>A wave of high-ranking women have left the Trump administration in the past year. Many were replaced by men.</article>

items.title: Democrats Took Over Texas. What Now?
items.author: Jess Bidgood
items.content: <article>Democrats’ wins in the Lone Star state exceeded their wildest dreams.</article>

items.title: Susie Wiles, Trump’s Chief of Staff, Is Accused of Blocking Health Policies to Attract Donations
items.author: Christina Jewett and Sheryl Gay Stolberg
items.content: <article>In a no-holds-barred interview with Joe Rogan, Calley Means, a former top health adviser, accused Susie Wiles of repeatedly bowing to lobbying pressures and fixating on campaign contributions.</article>

items.title: Hegseth Faces Impeachment Effort and Bipartisan Scrutiny After Midterm Elections
items.author: Helene Cooper, Greg Jaffe and Eric Schmitt
items.content: <article>A looming impeachment push could put President Trump’s polarizing defense secretary in a standoff with Democrats and Republicans.</article>

items.title: How Elon Musk Frittered Away Nearly $500 Million on the Midterm Elections
items.author: Theodore Schleifer
items.content: <article>Behind the scenes, the world’s richest person spent a record amount over two years to bend the country’s politics to his will. He couldn’t.</article>

items.title: Christopher Murphy Will Not Return to Senate Next Week After Stroke
items.author: Michael Gold
items.content: <article>Senator Christopher S. Murphy, Democrat of Connecticut, said in a statement that he would spend several weeks recovering at a rehabilitation center.</article>

items.title: Amazon Follows Melania Trump Film With Two-Part Series by the Same Director
items.author: Marc Tracy
items.content: <article>The documentary, which the first lady executive produces, will debut on Nov. 20. Brett Ratner directs.</article>

items.title: U.S. Attorney Who Oversaw Centerpiece of Trump’s Revenge Campaign Resigns
items.author: Devlin Barrett, Glenn Thrush and Alan Feuer
items.content: <article>Jason Reding Quiñones joins what is expected to be a succession of departures at the Justice Department after the midterm elections, including that of the leader of the national security division.</article>

items.title: U.S. Global Health Strategy Jeopardizes Prevention of Pandemics, Experts Warn
items.author: Apoorva Mandavilli
items.content: <article>The Trump administration has been negotiating agreements with dozens of individual countries. Public health experts say a global agreement would be far more effective.</article>

items.title: John D. Rockefeller IV, West Virginia Governor and Senator, Dies at 89
items.author: Robert D. McFadden
items.content: <article>The rare Democrat in a fabled family of wealthy Republicans, he served 30 years as senator and helped bring health insurance to millions of low-income children.</article>

items.title: Melania Trump Repositions the White Suit
items.author: Vanessa Friedman
items.content: <article>The first lady wore a white suit to preside over the White House meeting of delegations from Russia and Ukraine.</article>
